ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-01.prompt: Find the value of $$\frac{\text{the sum of the first nine prime numbers}}{(\text{the sum of the first three prime numbers})^2}.$$

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-02.prompt: $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with $AB = BC$. A point $D$ can be placed on the side $AB$ between $A$ and $B$ such that $AC = CD = DB$. What is the size, in degrees, of $\angle ABC$?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-03.prompt:
The integers $a$, $b$ and $c$ have the following properties:

- $a$, $b$ and $c$ are all prime numbers with $a<b<c$,
- the sum of $a$, $b$ and $c$ is $42$,
- the sum of the differences, $c-a$, $c-b$ and $b-a$ is also $42$.

What is the value of $b$?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-04.prompt: The first term of a sequence is $0.8$. Each subsequent term of the sequence is half the sum of all the earlier terms in the sequence. How many terms of the sequence are less than $2$?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-05.prompt: A grandmother set aside some money to give to each of her four grandchildren and her favourite charity. The grandmother gave Alison half of her money. Then she gave Bertie a third of what remained. Next she gave a quarter of what now remained to Charlotte. Finally she gave a fifth of what now remained to Desmond. The grandmother now found that she was left with exactly £1440 to give to charity. How much money, in total, did the grandmother give to her four grandchildren?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-06.prompt: Patricia has two red balls and a yellow ball inside a bag. Quentin has two yellow balls and a green ball inside a bag. Rosemary has two green balls and a red ball inside a bag. Without looking, Patricia, Quentin and Rosemary each take a ball from their bag. What is the probability that no two balls picked from the bags are the same colour? Give your answer in the form $\frac ab$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers with no common factor other than 1.

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-07.prompt: A newspaper consists of several large sheets of paper stacked together and then folded in half. Each large sheet of paper has four pages of the newspaper printed on it. On each large sheet the total of the four page numbers printed on it is $90$. How many large sheets of paper make up the newspaper?

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-08.prompt: In how many ways can $45$ be expressed as the sum of (at least two) consecutive positive integers? The order of the numbers in the sum does not matter. For example, $22+23$ would count as being the same as $23+22$.

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-09.prompt: A rhombus $ABCD$ is drawn in which $\angle BCD$ is $60^\circ$. A circle is inscribed in the rhombus so that it touches each side of the rhombus. The area of the circle is $12\pi\ \text{cm}^2$. What is the area of the rhombus in $\text{cm}^2$? Give your answer in the form $a\sqrt p$, where $a$ is an integer and $p$ is prime.

ukmt-stmc-2018-19-regional-group-10.prompt: Zebedee needs to choose a five-digit passcode for his new phone. Zebedee wants all five digits to be different and non-zero. Zebedee also wants to have at least two square digits in his passcode and at least two prime digits in his passcode. How many of these passcodes are there?
